title: Non-deterministic stream normalizer & contract assertor for multi-lang SDKs
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Build a cassette-less testing adapter and contract runner that lets Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs run deterministic acceptance tests against streaming endpoints without brittle timestamp/order/size assumptions.

Context: Existing fixtures rely on recorded 'cassettes' and replay servers that often break when chunk boundaries, backpressure, or retry semantics change. SDK engineers need a tool that normalizes real traffic into canonical frames, reproduces network jitter/reorder scenarios on demand, and asserts API contract compatibility across language SDKs and runtime bundlings.

This ticket scops: prototype a lightweight proxy (local dev/CI) that can: (1) ingest live traffic to produce sanitized deterministic fixtures, (2) playback canonicalized fixtures with configurable jitter/reorder/forking, (3) assert frame-level contracts with fuzzy token-level comparisons and schema assertions, and (4) expose simple per-language test adapters for Python/TS/Go that integrate with existing SDK test suites.
tasks: Design canonical streaming frame format and normalization rules (chunk coalescing, metadata stripping, content hashing)
Implement a minimal replay proxy (Go service) that accepts a TCP/TLS upstream and logs normalized frames
Add sanitizer plugins: obfuscate API keys, redact PII, canonicalize timestamps/UUIDs
Playback engine: support configurable latency/jitter, out-of-order frames, partial chunk drops, and forked responses to exercise retry logic
Create Python/TS/Go test adapters that translate SDK streaming iterators/callbacks to/from the canonical frame format
Write contract assertions: JSON schema checks, permissible delta rules for text generation, and token-level fuzzy match thresholds
End-to-end CI job that runs the contract suite against live staging Redwood endpoints nightly
Documentation & examples: regenerate fixtures from a captured session and add quickstart for SDK engineers
acceptance_criteria: Proxy can ingest a 1-min sample of staging streaming traffic and produce a deterministic fixture that replays identically on CI when normalization enabled
Playback engine can introduce reorder/jitter and trigger at least three SDK retry code paths in Python/TS/Go tests
Contract runner flags schema violations and reports token-level regression scores; PR gating pipeline fails on regressions above threshold
Sanitizer removes secrets and preserves breadcrumbs needed for debugging (request IDs, model versions) without leaking customer data
Adapters present a 1-line fixture load call for each language and integrate with existing SDK unit test harnesses
technical_notes: Canonical frame model: {event_type:string, seq:int, payload_b64:string, meta:{model:string, truncated:bool, req_id:string, ts_iso:string}} - note: meta must be flattened into strings in JSON fixture
Normalization steps: re-chunk to max 16KB boundaries, minimize contiguous whitespace, strip ephemeral timing fields, replace UUIDs with deterministic tokens using per-fixture seed
Playback variants: replay-fast (no delays), replay-realistic (preserve original inter-frame gaps), replay-chaos (random reorder/drop) - expose via playback profile header
Fuzzy comparison: use normalized Levenshtein for text frames with configurable threshold per-model; exact match for control frames (e.g., model selection, error codes)
Proxy implementation note: Go is preferred for low-overhead gobetween; provide Docker image for CI. Python/TS adapters can be thin wrappers calling proxy API over localhost socket
Idempotency testing: provide ability to fork responses mid-stream to verify SDKs deduplicate/merge streamed chunks correctly
Security: ensure sanitizer runs before any fixture leaves developer machine; CI must run sanitizer again as a safety step
Performance: proxy should handle 200 concurrent streaming sessions in local CI runners (benchmark target)
